purpose: baseline of 0.6.x (stored-result diagnostics; release gates use the interleaved A/B against the 0.5.1 source tree)
methodology: schema 2.2, Harness V3 (5 warm-ups, 3 x 7 batches, >= 50 ms per sample, median-of-medians), median of three complete runs (tools/ace-repeatability0.6.0.py), interleaved A/B vs the 0.5.1 source tree (3 batches per side, alternating order)

verdict.repeatability: pass, deterministic values identical over 3 runs x 28 families; macro spread <= 5 % (compression, observed maximum 2.7 %) / <= 15 % (decompression, observed maximum 9.9 %)
verdict.ab_vs_0_5_1: pass, 12 / 12 cases, byte-identical output; speed ratios 0.993 - 1.044 (all cases >= 0.993)

allocation: mixed_16x256k engine bytes per input byte: Fast 5.9, Balanced 8.3 (0.5.1: 16.1), Dense 11.1 (0.5.1: 24.3); int-sparse-change Balanced 5.9 (0.5.1: 35.7)
files: benchmark-0.6.0-<family>.json (families incl. regression and repeatability; public-corpus is empty, ACE_PUBLIC_CORPUS was not set), ab-0.6.0-vs-0.5.1.json, and the 0.5.1 allocation-profile / float-false-positive documents used as comparison, unchanged from the run
note: reference run of the 0.6.0 release on the author's workstation (performance governor, 37 C); the stored_baseline and lz4 / zstd drift rows are diagnostics against the 0.5.1 results. Compared with 0.5.1 the stricter-decoder slowdown of dense decode is gone and encode is 0.985 - 1.044 of 0.5.1.
